clue.text: After damage, no longer use one shed

indicators.note: After puts the second piece behind the first, so the word for giving up follows the word for damage

parts.note: to tear something is to damage it
to drop a habit or a thing is to stop using it

explanation.surface: Someone has broken a tool and decides to abandon the shed it lives in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden hut but is the past participle of shedding a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop of liquid wept from the eye is exactly one tear that has been shed.

clue.text: Not right for sculptor to make a god

indicators.note: Not right asks for the abbreviation R, for right, to be removed from the next piece

parts.note: Auguste Rodin was the French sculptor of The Thinker

explanation.surface: A sculptor wrongly attempts to carve a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not right' reads as a moral judgement but means drop the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief deity of Norse mythology, father of Thor.

clue.text: State of a chess champion spoken about

indicators.note: spoken about tells us the phrase is to be heard rather than read, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the indefinite article, A; Emanuel Lasker was world chess champion from 1894 to 1921

explanation.surface: Gossip about the condition of a chess title-holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' reads as 'condition' in the surface; it is a US state. Non-rhotic British speech makes 'a Lasker' match it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is the largest of the fifty United States, so an example of a state.

clue.text: Short book of words about beer that not all may understand

definitions.note: a relative phrase standing for a noun: speech that outsiders may not follow

indicators.note: about means the dictionary abbreviation goes around the beer
Short means the dictionary is cut down to its usual abbreviation

parts.note: a dictionary is a book of words
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A pocket dictionary about beer full of jargon that baffles outsiders.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase rather than a synonym, leaning on the surface's 'words'.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional form of a language has local vocabulary and pronunciation that speakers from elsewhere may not follow.

clue.text: Sort of belt in vehicle — a girl is knocked over

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: knocked over, in a down clue, means the girl's name is turned upside down, reading bottom to top

parts.note: Nell is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl gets hit by a van and knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is knocked over' reverses NELL to LLEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Van Allen belts are zones of charged particles trapped by Earth's magnetic field.

clue.text: English currency Scotsman holds in error — such mysteries

indicators.note: holds in means the first group of letters keeps the error inside it

parts.note: the leu is the currency of Romania
Ian is a typically Scottish name, standing for a Scotsman
a sin is a moral error

explanation.surface: A Scot mistakenly hangs on to some English money in a puzzling affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds in' means the outer chain keeps the error inside; LEU is the Romanian currency unit, and the definition leans on the clue's 'such' to make the answer an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eleusinian Mysteries were secret initiation rites of ancient Greece, held at Eleusis for Demeter and Persephone.

clue.text: Cyclist punched by a surprise assailant

indicators.note: punched by means the cyclist is pierced by the letter, which sits inside

parts.note: a rider on a bicycle is a cyclist

explanation.surface: A cyclist is assaulted by a mugger jumping out at him.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider makes a sudden attack, typically one the victim does not expect.

clue.text: This may suggest I held capital

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer says take a fresh arrangement of five letters, and that rearrangement yields the clue's two words I HELD

explanation.surface: Someone boasting that they once had money in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: NEW is the anagram signal and DELHI the fodder, whose letters remake I HELD.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the seat of India's government, so the country's capital.

clue.text: On the surface, some accommodation is empty

parts.note: some, as in 'some room', gives the article A

indicators.note: is here reads as 'has in it', so the accommodation holds the empty letter

parts.note: a flat is an apartment, a form of accommodation
O, a round zero, stands for nothing or empty

explanation.surface: On the face of it, the lodging on offer is vacant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the surface' looks like 'apparently' but is floating on water.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating boat rests on top of the water rather than sinking.

clue.text: Country poetically taking sheep to its heart

indicators.note: to its heart cuts the sheep breed down to its core, losing the outer letters

parts.note: the merino is a breed of sheep prized for fine wool

explanation.surface: A nation in verse embraces its flocks.
explanation.walkthrough: The sheep is trimmed: only the heart of MERINO is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the old poetic name for Ireland, used in verse and song.

clue.text: Mixed salad prepared in island (Guam)

indicators.note: prepared, as a dish is made up, signals the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A salad made up on a Pacific island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guam' in brackets looks like an aside about the island; both words are fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Salmagundi is an old dish of chopped meat, eggs and vegetables, a mixed salad.

clue.text: Doctor accepts criticism, taking a strong drink

indicators.note: accepts means the doctor takes the criticism inside

parts.note: GP, general practitioner, is a family doctor
a rap is a rebuke or criticism, as in a rap on the knuckles

explanation.surface: A doctor takes a telling-off and reaches for a stiff drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappa is a potent Italian brandy distilled from grape residue.

clue.text: An occasion in early spring when uplands may flourish

indicators.note: flourish suggests the letters are waved about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Hills burst into bloom at the start of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may' looks like a verb but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sunday before Easter, falling in March or April, commemorates Christ's entry into Jerusalem.

clue.text: Be prone to run into officers in ships

indicators.note: into means the lying and running letters go inside the officers

parts.note: COL is short for colonel, so COLS are officers
to be prone is to lie flat
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Naval officers tend to dash round their vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a cargo vessel built to carry coal.

clue.text: Plentiful work endlessly offered by library

indicators.note: endlessly means the piece of work loses its final letter

parts.note: an opus is a musical or literary work
a library lends books, so what it offered was lent

explanation.surface: A library generously loans out an unending supply of books.
explanation.definitionFit: Something opulent is lavish and abundant, rich in quantity.

clue.text: A short denial

definitions.meaning: read cryptically, a person who is short is one who is ... one

explanation.surface: A brief refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NOT A TALL, the phrase describes someone short.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a strong refusal or negation, meaning 'in no way'.

clue.text: Call to be silent — it leaves some out

indicators.note: some ... out means a portion of the following words is brought out from inside them

explanation.surface: An order to keep quiet, with a note that it omits some details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it leaves some out' looks like a comment on the clue but is the extraction signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle a book is to name it, just as one might call it something.

clue.text: Large cubes seen floating about in drink he supplies?

definitions.note: a person described by a clause: the one who supplies drink

parts.note: ice comes in cubes, as in a drink

indicators.note: floating about suggests the letters drift around into a new order

explanation.surface: Big ice cubes bobbing in a drink served by a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's licensee holds the permit to sell alcohol, so is the one in charge of serving it.

clue.text: Guide for the night has no shelter to sleep, clutching short black coat

indicators.note: clutching means the outer letters hold the coat inside them
has no means the shelter is taken out of the word sleep

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

indicators.note: short means the coat word loses its last letter

parts.note: tarmac is the black coating laid on roads

explanation.surface: A homeless sleeper in a cropped dark jacket needs a guide through the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no shelter' reads as homelessness but takes LEE out, leaving SP; 'short' trims the road coat to TARMA, which 'clutching' puts inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart of constellations helps a viewer find their way around the night sky.

clue.text: Winger spoils shot, receiving tackle from in front

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil it

indicators.note: receiving means the shot takes the next letter inside

parts.note: a hit is a shot that strikes

indicators.note: from in front picks out the leading letter of the word tackle

explanation.surface: A football winger fluffs a shot after being tackled from the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' looks like a footballer but is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The marsh tit is a small European bird, and any bird is a winged creature.

clue.text: Lion tamer's head not straight

parts.note: Aslan is the lion in C. S. Lewis's Narnia stories

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A lion tamer's head is tilted to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lying aslant is slanting or at an angle, not upright.

clue.text: Noisily eat all round one city

indicators.note: all round means the eating word goes around the number one

parts.note: to munch is to chew audibly
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone chomps loudly through a meal around a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Munich is the capital of Bavaria in southern Germany.

clue.text: Hothead's plan to arrest officer

indicators.note: to arrest means the plan catches the officer and holds him inside

parts.note: a map is a plan of an area
ADC, aide-de-camp, is an officer assisting a general

explanation.surface: A rash person's scheme to detain a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap is a reckless, impulsive person who acts without thinking.

clue.text: Mean to take double-length science magazine among papers

indicators.note: among means the letters go in among the papers

parts.note: ID, identity documents, are papers

indicators.note: double means the length abbreviation is written twice over

parts.note: Nature is a leading scientific journal

explanation.surface: A plan to sneak an extended science journal among one's papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A mean person is spiteful and unkind, of bad temper or character.

clue.text: Free cover includes at first nearly all there

indicators.note: includes means the cover takes the picked letter inside

parts.note: an SAE, stamped addressed envelope, is a cover the recipient gets free to reply in

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of nearly

explanation.surface: A free envelope in which almost everything is present.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all there is an idiom for being of sound mind, the opposite of mad.

clue.text: So Tom's called for this milk

indicators.note: called, as in calling out, means a word heard aloud that matches

parts.note: Tom Sawyer is Mark Twain's boy hero, so Tom's surname

explanation.surface: A child named Tom asks for a particular milk.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the surname Sawyer is said like the bean.
explanation.definitionFit: Soya milk is a plant-based drink made from soybeans, an alternative to dairy.

clue.text: Awaiting summons from head of court in plain wrapper, to be returned

indicators.note: to be returned means the whole assembled piece reads backwards
in places the picked letter inside the plain
wrapper means the plain wraps round the letter

parts.note: a llano is a grassy plain in South America

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of court

explanation.surface: A court summons arriving in a plain envelope, to be sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside LLANO, giving LLACNO, which is then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who is on call is available and waiting to be summoned if needed.

clue.text: One that breaks down, as nearly mad

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters have gone wild and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone breaking down, almost insane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks down' suggests a nervous collapse; the answer breaks things into parts.
explanation.definitionFit: An analyser takes something apart into its components to examine it.
